title: Supabase Raises $150M, Agrees to Buy Turso
key_facts: On 2 Oct 2026 SiliconANGLE reported Supabase raised $150 million in a round led by GIC, with CapitalG, IronArc and SquarePeg, and agreed to buy Turso for an undisclosed sum.
The round size is not the purchase price.
CEO Paul Copplestone wrote 'For existing users, nothing changes' and put Supabase's pace at more than one million database launches per week.
Turso keeps working on SQLite, Supabase on Postgres; Turso's SQLite rewrite targets server workloads, including concurrent writes.
The new capital is intended partly for employee liquidity and partly for features aimed at AI agents.
No migration workflow or compatibility guarantee from Turso to Supabase Postgres has been released; deeper integration is expected in the coming months.
Turso founder Glauber Costa becomes Head of Agentic Services; cofounder Pekka Enberg and colleagues join Supabase.
quote_evidence: The financing and acquisition were disclosed together, but the amount raised is not the purchase price.
The undisclosed purchase price makes it impossible to calculate a transaction multiple or infer how much of the financing will support the deal.
A path into the Supabase ecosystem is part of the plan, but no migration workflow or compatibility guarantee has been released.
why_it_matters_hint: A Postgres platform is buying a maker of small SQLite databases to serve the many databases AI agents create.
notes: Event is a week old (2 Oct 2026); Quasa.io is a secondary outlet relaying SiliconANGLE and Supabase's own post; score lowered by 2 as stale.
